links.reason: Verse 93 has the king say sending the captive before the elephant would be பெரும்பழி, having admitted பொய்யினிற் றந்த; the claim that he 'ignores' the lie is an inference, the verse states it. Kural 652 is advice to ministers on acts yielding neither fame nor good, so the pairing is a loose fit.

நிரைத்த தீவினை நீங்க (1603) and பணிவாரருவினை தீர்க்கும் (910) share the idea that a hill removes karma, but 910 is flagged garbled and the 'doctrinal quarrel over how deeds are destroyed' is not in either text; the gains clauses are generic.
Verse 317 itself says இதுபொழுது உய்ம்மின், so the epic does not lack urgency as the gains clause says; the link is only a shared theme of renunciation, with the verse's sense flagged uncertain.

Naga 4 says gathered deeds can be shed கணத்தினில் (sense uncertain); Naladiyar 101 says the old deed seeks its doer but not that it cannot be shed, and the Naladiyar is itself a Jain book, so 'the Jain account' as an exit against it is overstated.

1121 is a threat to brand Civakan கள்வர்; 1165 is praise of him believing him dead. These are not incompatible claims about one thing, so TENSION does not fit; the ironic contrast is real but the plot already records it.

Only the name Chandika joins them: Yasodhara 137 has a mother urging a kid sacrificed to a folk goddess, while Tirumanthiram 1050 describes the Devi's form (கொலைவிற் புருவத்தள்) and mentions no offering, so the gains claim that its Chandika receives the offering is false.

Line 1627 fears an unnamed woman (marker thinks Tattai) will die; 1530 shows Kemasari holding back her life. Identifying the woman as Kemasari is not in the Tamil and neither verse makes a claim the other contradicts.

1428 follows 1427 in story order; the spirits saying they will fill their bellies (பெருவயிறு ஆர்தும்) is plot sequence, and 'destruction as a feast that feeds many' is the note's gloss, not a development.

303 shows Vijayai's fall as proof of sin (காட்டுவாள் போல); 2625 has a preacher cite a ruined woman crying அந்தோ வினையே. Both use a ruined woman as a lesson, but 'draw on one fund of images' is only a shared theme.

908 fixes the vow (Civakan alone may break her seclusion) and 2036 has the women moved by the song and praising the youth she wrought in mind (காளை நாமம் வாழ்த்துவார்); the fulfilment is only hinted and 'unrecognised' is the note's inference.
1792 (eyes fall on the prince and leave the kings) follows 1791 directly; 'proof by where onlookers look' is a thin gloss on consecutive description.

1151 refers back to the diamond pillar of 1139 (வயிரத் திண்டூண் ... எரிந்து கிடந்த), so the callback is real, but it is plot continuity the graph already records; 'burned' vs 'shattered' is not exact.

Both lovers refuse to blink: 1122 (இமைப்பின் ... ஏதிலாள் போலும்; gaze unblinking) and Kural 1129 (இமைப்பின் கரப்பாக்கு ... ஏதிலர்). The shared word ஏதில் and the different reason (she recedes at each blink vs he hides) make the pairing specific and both gains clauses true.

1386 states honour as going forward against spears (மானமாம்); Kural 774 is the laugh at pulling a spear from one's body. The note itself says the epic hero shows no wound-joy, so the 'gains' is something the verse lacks; only a shared theme of the brave soldier.

Kural 555 has the tears of the oppressed wear away wealth; Sil 20:100-103 has the king die at Kannaki's sight and words (காண்டளவே தோற்றான் ... உயிர்). Instant death of a king at one wronged woman's words contrasts with slow wearing, but this is a case of the rule, nearer QUALIFIES.

Both have a searcher asking அந்தணிர் on the waste road and the answer கண்டனெம்; but 'Kalittokai expanded Ainkurunuru' is an unsupported claim of dependence and 'testimony grew into doctrine' overstates it.

1092 has the belting of Civakan's shoulders (கச்சின் வீக்கலின்) and 16 the god removing the பூங் கச்சு that bound them, a real pairing; but 'grateful god' is not in 16 (the god is unnamed) and the eclipse 'promise' is the note's gloss.

Naladiyar 3 names ஏனை வினை as the cause of the kings' fall; 797 shows umbrellas overturned by Civakan's arrows, and neither says what the note adds: 799 is not in the packet and the 'impermanence lesson' is not in 797 (flagged uncertain).

Naga 166 gives siddhi to the two by yoga and heaven to the rest by austerity; Tirumanthiram 258 names two ways (தவம், அறம்) as a boat over வினைக்கடல். The epic's two ends are not 'the same austerity reaching two shores', so teaches and gains do not hold.

Both use a bubble in rain (மாரி மொக்குளின் / படுமழை மொக்குளின்) and the epic shows the teacher's release after severing desire, which is the resolve the quatrain praises. But the epic's bubble marks a clean end, and reading in 'repeated birth' is the note's addition.

214 has பூமிசை ஒதுங்கினை, the same sense as Kural 3 மலர்மிசை ஏகினான், with no shared word, and line 3 is damaged; the verse's Lord is called போதியங் கிழவன். 'Borrowed' epithet is unproven, so the gains is not established.

2940 describes the body's colour fading (நிறங் கரக்குங் காலம்); Siddhar 23 is corrupt in line 2 and speaks of seeing one's own bones. Both treat the body's decay, but 'a loss and a practice' is a shared theme, not a development.

180 says the shrine does பிறவி தீர்ப்பன; Kural 10 says those who reach the Lord's feet cross the sea of births. The 'qualification' (shrine vs devotee's reaching) is a thin contrast; the verse is flagged for sense.

2962 asks துறத்தல் தகவாமோ (is renouncing fitting); Naladiyar 56 says it is hard (அருமை) to put away a wife to argue that marriage is a burden. Different points, so the 'bond cannot be cast off' agreement is stretched.

Both poems report as eyewitness the enemy's wasted land (கண்டனென் வருவல் / கண்டுவந் திசினே) and mark it with white velai (வேளை வெண்பூ / வெண்பூ வேளை). Patitruppattu 15 then adds a second sight of the king's own land (நீபுறந் தருதலின் ... யாணர்நன் நாடுங் கண்டு), so the extension claim holds.
2602 has இல்லையே கைம்மாறு said by the queen, close to Kural 101's repayment beyond earth and heaven; but this is the Kural's rule illustrated, and the 'gains' clauses are muddled.

1939 says the torments are வினையின் விளைவு with no judge named; Tirumanthiram 2544 says the Lord set hell by grace but also ends with வினையுயிர் பெற்றதே, so the claim that it gives no cause in the sufferer's deed is false; the TM verse is flagged uncertain.

Both give heavenly brides to the warrior who dies (2302 கடியர மகளிர்த் தோய்வர்; PN 287 மாசில் மகளிர் மன்றல் ... உயர்நிலை உலகத்து நுகர்ப). But 'survival of the Sangam promise into the epic' is unproven, and the other-side gain is a judgment the poem does not draw.
Both show gods covering the sky with flowers and sandal, a stock motif. The note's 'end of the war' vs 'teaching' contrast is not shown by 2121, which names no war.
1576 has the jester run to the king with mouth watering; 1618 is a yamaka song of his heart at the fruits. The 'pardon' the note says his greed pays for is not in either verse.
2847 lists the four endless qualities of the liberated; Kural 362 is advice to desire release by desiring nothing. The 'emptying versus filling' contrast treats a method as a description of release.

2607 says the eight wives came in the night's dream as a crown of eight garlands (எண் கோதைத் தொகை ... கங்குற் கனவகத்தே), answering the dream of 223 (எண் முத்து அணி மாலை முடிக்கு இடனாக ... முளை). A dream fulfilled, and the note names the right words.

1891 closely follows Kural 828 (தொழுத கையினுள்ளும் ... அழுத கண்ணீரினுள்ளும்) and adds hair and caskets; but 'a bodyguard's order' and 'against poisoning' are not in the Tamil, which names படை (weapons) and is a warning by Nandattan.
Kural 200 asks for useful speech; 291 defines truth as harmless speech. Two chapters setting different standards is not an incompatible claim about the same thing.
382 says the teacher taught இல்லறத்து இயல்பு; Kural 49 calls household life virtue. That the epic holds household virtue 'as a stage' is the note's inference, and the verse is flagged uncertain.

Both compare giving to water (36 flood carrying wealth to the needy; Kural 215 wealth like the village tank). The claim that the image 'ran both ways in the tradition' is unsupported and 36 is flagged uncertain.
3036 and 945 are about the mantra at death (இறக்கின்ற போழ்தில், செவிச் செப்புகின்றான்); the dog's rebirth as Sutanjanan and his praise are not in either verse and both are flagged uncertain.
1462 shows the king's fall and 1464 has onlookers say நிலையாமை சால நிலைபெற்றது; a scene and its moral, in story order with the graph already recording the sequence.

180 describes the animal births as a bare event (the verse says nothing of deeds or the mother's motive); casting the pursuer as the 'shadow' of the doer's deed (Kural 208) depends on the reconstructed plot, and the Kural's shadow is a consequence, not a pursuer.
2259 shows Nabulan refusing to strike (வேழமும் எறிதல் செல்லான்) and 2261 states the code, which is real; but 'how this whole company fights' goes beyond 2261, which describes one அயிலுழவன்.

539 names Rajamapuram from the horoscope and 11 mentions the defeat at the vina; the note's claim that the prophecy 'sends the princess to earth' and starts the contest is reconstruction, and 11 is flagged uncertain.

182 shows fishers torturing the crocodile (கொலைவலாளர் குறைத்தனர்), but no deed is named, so Kural 320 (நோயெல்லாம் நோய்செய்தார் மேலவாம்) is applied from outside; 'adding to their own account' is not in the verse.

318 has Vijayai suckle the child and leave him with her husband's ring; 1910 has the grown son say அடியன் and fall at her feet (அடி தழுவி வீழ்ந்தான்). A separation and its reunion, with the servant-address noted in 1910.
